chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his father quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Zayd linked the hadith up to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family):

He said: A single dirham spent on dye is better than spending a thousand dirhams in the path of God. It has fourteen characteristics: it expels wind from the ears, clears the haze from the sight, softens the nostrils, improves the breath, strengthens the gums, eliminates weakness, and lessens the whispers of Satan. The angels rejoice in it. The believer takes glad tidings from it, and the disbeliever is enraged by it. It is an ornament and a scent, and a protection in his grave, and the questioning angels (Munkar and Nakir) feel shy of it.

key_terms.الْغَشَاوَةَ: Haze or film over the eyes
key_terms.مَنْكَرٌ وَنَكِيرٌ: The two angels who question the dead in the grave

ai.seo_question: What are the fourteen virtues of using henna or dye according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to emphasize the Sunnah of beautification (tajmil) as an act of worship, elevating the modest expenditure on henna above significant charitable spending due to its multifaceted benefits. The narration details fourteen specific virtues, blending physical hygiene—such as strengthening gums and improving eyesight—with spiritual protections, including repelling Satan's whispers and serving as a light for the soul in the grave before the questioning of Munkar and Nakir.
